refreshed_fact_check.intent_notes: Passes and does the job better than a generic answer. No claims are contradicted; two are unsupported but low-risk. Weakness: the main step for finding follower locations (Total followers → top locations, 100+ followers) is backed only by third-party guides (Zolyp, Instapect, Lilach Bullock), not by the linked Meta page. A Meta Business Help 'About Instagram Insights' page (facebook.com/business/help/788388387972460) may confirm it, but it couldn't be opened, so it wasn't treated as evidence. If an editor can confirm it, citing it would replace the second-hand wording. Map privacy gap: the article omits that location-tagged posts, reels and stories can appear on the Map for 24 hours even without location sharing. The specific-follower answer is also incomplete: it doesn't say you can see a follower's last active location on the Map if they choose to share it with you. Suggested addition: "Even without location sharing, posts, reels and stories you tag with a location can appear on the Map for people who follow you for 24 hours (Meta, 6 Aug 2025). And if a friend chooses to share their last active location with you, you'll see it there." Fixes in priority order: (1) add the Map point about location-tagged content; (2) cite Instapect for the 'switched back to personal' row; (3) soften or remove the 'yesterday's new followers' line; (4) optionally check and cite the Meta Business Help 'About Instagram Insights' page for the 100-follower top-locations rule.
refreshed_fact_check.value_notes: Strengths: it follows Meta's current rule (any public account) and explains why some guides still say business-only. It separates the 100-follower and 100-viewer thresholds, and the followers / viewers / engaged accounts groups, which most guides blur. The API limits (top 45, partial demographic data, 48-hour delay) explain why totals don't add up and are labelled as API-specific. The troubleshooting table matches the sources, and the Map section is accurate. Weaknesses: repetition (the Sprout 'more than 100 accounts reached' point appears twice and the Instapect 'owner-only' point three times), and the baking-business example is hypothetical, with no screenshots or real data.
refreshed_fact_check.product_notes: All four Instagramaps claims (audience by country and city, per-post comparison, marketplace, pricing of $0 Creator Free and Business Free plans with Creator Pro at $9/month) match the allowed claims and the live page. The disclosure ('built by the team behind New Earns') isn't among the allowed claims and can't be verified, but as a disclosure the reviewer would keep it. The article makes no extra product claims.
